_why: The 'zero then one' rows from ADR 0033 and ADR 0035, re-derived under
These are the highest-risk entries in the whole debt list. Each was
originally recorded NOT CAUGHT, then closed by a test written for it --
so each is a claim that a gap was fixed, made by a harness now known to
have been wrong three separate ways. If any table in this project is
going to disagree on re-derivation, it is one of these.
One set spanning two ADRs because they share a suite and the same
finding: a defensive branch the fixtures could not reach, tested at the
level where it CAN fail rather than deleted (ADR 0033/0045's rule).

mutations._note: Originally unreachable: `effector._presence_of` returns only 'present' or 'absent', so the third state its own docstring promises is never produced today. Reading silence as absence would manufacture a contrast against every unlabelled row in the pool -- the warning would fire constantly and be ignored.

mutations.description: only the base is checked, not the full tokens (ADR 0035)
mutations._note: The base of 'NADH' is the truncated 'NAD'. PubChem happens to know NAD, so the base check alone worked here -- and would have failed silently for the next acronym whose stem is not itself a catalogued compound.

mutations.description: a resolver exception counts as "is a compound" (ADR 0035)
mutations._note: The direction matters: returning True on failure suppresses the mixture warning, so a network blip silently turns a real finding off. Returning False keeps the warning and risks a false positive, which is the survivable direction.
mutations.find:
except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
        return False
mutations.replace:
except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
        return True
